skill.name: site-architecture
skill.description: Use when planning SEO-friendly site architecture, navigation, internal links, and page hierarchy so the agent follows the marketingskills playbook instead of producing generic marketing advice.
whenToUse: The user asks for help planning SEO-friendly site architecture, navigation, internal links, and page hierarchy
A marketing task needs product, audience, positioning, and channel context before execution
The agent should create a repeatable site architecture workflow instead of a one-off generic answer
The work needs clear success metrics, deliverables, and next steps for a growth or GTM motion

keyConcepts.explanation: Check for product marketing context first: If .agents/product-marketing.md exists (or .claude/product-marketing.md, or the legacy product-marketing-context.md filename, in older setups), read it before asking questions. Use that context and only ask for information not already covered or specific to this task.
What does the company do? Who are the primary audiences? What are the top 3 goals for the site? (conversions, SEO traffic, education, support)
New site or restructuring an existing one? If restructuring: what's broken? (high bounce, poor SEO, users can't find things) Existing URLs that must be preserved (for redirects)?
SaaS marketing site Content/blog site E-commerce Documentation Hybrid (SaaS + content) Small business / local
How many pages exist or are planned? What are the most important pages? (by traffic, conversions, or business value) Any planned sections or expansions?

Site Type Typical Depth Key Sections URL Pattern SaaS marketing 2-3 levels Home, Features, Pricing, Blog, Docs /features/name, /blog/slug Content/blog 2-3 levels Home, Blog, Categories, About /blog/slug, /category/slug

apiReference.purpose: Install the site-architecture skill from coreyhaines31/marketingskills.

gotchas: Do not add pages only because keywords exist; each page needs a distinct search intent and conversion path.
Internal links should reflect hierarchy and user journeys, not just distribute PageRank mechanically.
Read product-marketing context first when present; otherwise the agent may ask repeated setup questions or make weak positioning assumptions.
Do not ship generic best practices without tying recommendations to the product, audience, channel, and conversion goal.
Separate strategy from execution: clarify the campaign decision before drafting assets or implementation steps.
